questions.question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get per year?
questions.answer: Full-time employees accrue 16 days of annual leave per calendar year under the current Leave Policy v2.[1]
questions.expected: 16 days (Leave Policy v2, which supersedes v1's 12 days).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the current v2 entitlement of 16 days per calendar year, matching the reference and evidence.

questions.question: How much vacation do I get?
questions.answer: Full-time employees in the United States accrue 16 days of annual leave per calendar year, credited each pay period in equal parts. Part-time employees accrue pro rata.[1]
questions.expected: 16 days of annual leave per calendar year.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the reference entitlement of 16 days of annual leave per calendar year and adds only supported details.

questions.question: How many sick days do employees get a year?
questions.answer: Employees receive 8 days of sick leave per year.[1]
questions.expected: 8 days of sick leave per year.
questions.judge_reason: The answer states the reference key fact that employees get 8 sick leave days per year and is supported by the in-force policy.

questions.question: How many unused leave days can I carry into next year, and when do they expire?
questions.answer: You can carry forward up to 8 unused annual leave days into the next calendar year. Those carried days must be used by March 31 or they lapse.[1]
questions.expected: Up to 8 days; they must be used by March 31.
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the in-force policy and the reference: up to 8 days can be carried forward and they expire if not used by March 31.

questions.question: Who needs to approve leave of more than ten consecutive working days?
questions.answer: Leave of more than ten consecutive working days needs approval from the employee’s direct manager in the HR portal and also the department head’s approval.[1]
questions.expected: The direct manager and also the department head.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives both required approvers: the direct manager and the department head.

questions.question: How long before a scheduled release does the deploy freeze start?
questions.answer: The deploy freeze starts 72 hours before every scheduled release.[1]
questions.expected: 72 hours (the deprecated 2023 runbook said 36 hours).
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the in-force runbook and the reference: the freeze starts 72 hours before a scheduled release.

questions.question: How long after a deploy can I use the one-click rollback?
questions.answer: You can use the one-click rollback for 45 minutes after full rollout completes.[1] The meeting notes also confirm the rollback window stays at 45 minutes.[2]
questions.expected: 45 minutes after full rollout completes (2023 runbook said 10 minutes).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the current 45-minute rollback window after full rollout completes, matching the in-force runbook and reference.

questions.question: How many approving reviews does a change to a production repository need?
questions.answer: A change to a production repository needs 2 approving reviews from someone other than the author before merge, plus a green CI pipeline.[1]
questions.expected: 2 approving reviews from someone other than the author, plus green CI.
questions.judge_reason: The answer exactly matches the cited in-force guideline and the reference: 2 non-author approvals plus green CI.

questions.question: How long does the canary stage run and how much traffic does it get?
questions.answer: The canary stage runs for ten minutes at 5 percent of traffic.[1]
questions.expected: Ten minutes at 5 percent of traffic.
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the cited in-force runbook and the reference: ten minutes at 5 percent traffic.

questions.question: How many weeks of paid leave do secondary caregivers get?
questions.answer: Secondary caregivers get 12 weeks of fully paid leave under the policy in force today.[1] For births and adoptions on or after 2027-01-01, this will increase to 26 weeks fully paid.[2]
questions.expected: 12 weeks today; 26 weeks for births/adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.
questions.judge_reason: The answer states the current 12-week entitlement and the scheduled 26-week entitlement for births/adoptions on or after 2027-01-01, matching the reference.

questions.question: My partner is due in March 2027. How much paid leave will I get as the secondary caregiver?
questions.answer: For a March 2027 birth, you will get 26 weeks of fully paid leave as the secondary caregiver, assuming the birth is on or after 2027-01-01.[1] The 2027 revision also says the leave may be split into two blocks within the first twelve months.[2]
questions.expected: 26 weeks fully paid (2027 revision applies to births on or after 2027-01-01).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the reference key fact that the 2027 revision applies to March 2027 births and provides 26 weeks fully paid leave for secondary caregivers.

questions.question: How much leave does a birth parent get?
questions.answer: A birth parent gets 16 weeks of fully paid leave. Up to four weeks may be taken before the expected due date.[1] The 2027 revision is not yet in effect, and it says birth parent leave will remain unchanged at 16 weeks.[2]
questions.expected: 16 weeks of fully paid leave.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the reference key fact—16 weeks of fully paid leave—and the extra details are supported and not contradictory.

questions.question: What is the maximum hotel room rate per night in San Francisco?
questions.answer: The maximum hotel room rate per night in San Francisco is $275, excluding taxes, because San Francisco is a Tier 1 city and Tier 1’s cap is $275 per night.[1][2]
questions.expected: $275 (San Francisco is Tier 1).
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the reference: San Francisco is Tier 1 and the Tier 1 hotel cap is $275 per night.

questions.question: What's the nightly hotel cap when I travel to Austin?
questions.answer: Austin is not listed in Tier 1 or Tier 2, so it falls under Tier 3; the nightly hotel cap is $150 before taxes.[1][2]
questions.expected: $150: Austin is not listed, so it falls in Tier 3.
questions.judge_reason: The answer correctly identifies Austin as an unlisted city in Tier 3 and gives the $150 pre-tax nightly hotel cap.

questions.question: What is the maximum fare for a one-way domestic flight?
questions.answer: The maximum fare for a one-way domestic flight is $450. A higher fare may be approved by the on-call manager in VoyageHub if the trip is booked less than 48 hours before departure for an incident response.[1]
questions.expected: $450, unless booked under 48 hours before departure for incident response.
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the policy limit and its stated incident-response exception.

questions.question: What is the daily per diem for an L3 employee travelling to Chicago?
questions.answer: The daily per diem for an L3 employee travelling to Chicago is $75. Chicago is Tier 2, and the Per-Diem Table lists L3, Tier 2 at $75.[1][2]
questions.expected: $75 (Chicago is tier 2).
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the reference: Chicago is Tier 2 and the L3 Tier 2 per diem is $75.

questions.question: Per diem for grade L2 in Boise?
questions.answer: The per diem for grade L2 in Boise is $50. Boise is listed in city tier 3, and the L2 tier 3 per diem is $50.[1]
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the reference and is directly supported by the cited in-force per-diem table.

questions.question: Do I need to file an expense claim to get my per diem?
questions.answer: No. Per-diem allowances are paid in advance when the trip is booked in VoyageHub, and no expense claim is needed for them.[1] The Travel Policy also says the per-diem covers meals and local transport and does not need receipts.[2]
questions.expected: No. Per diem is paid in advance when the trip is booked in VoyageHub; no claim is needed.
questions.judge_reason: The answer directly matches the reference: per diem is paid in advance through VoyageHub booking and no expense claim is needed.

questions.question: Who has to approve an expense claim of $4,000?
questions.answer: A $4,000 expense claim must be approved by your direct manager and a Vice President, unless it is travel booked through VoyageHub; VoyageHub-booked travel is pre-approved at booking time and needs only manager sign-off at claim time.[1]
questions.expected: A Vice President, in addition to the direct manager (unless it is VoyageHub-booked travel).
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the in-force policy: claims above $2,500 need manager and VP approval, with the stated VoyageHub-booked travel exception.

questions.question: I booked a $3,200 trip through VoyageHub. Does the claim need VP approval?
questions.answer: No. A $3,200 trip booked through VoyageHub does not need VP approval; VoyageHub travel is pre-approved at booking and needs only manager sign-off at claim time.[1] Also, the booking guide says VoyageHub travel does not need a separate expense claim or VP approval.[2]
questions.expected: No: VoyageHub travel is pre-approved at booking and needs only manager sign-off (the approval matrix alone would suggest VP).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the key exception that VoyageHub travel over $2,500 is pre-approved and needs only manager sign-off, not VP approval.

questions.question: How long does Finance take to process an approved expense claim?
questions.answer: Finance processes an approved expense claim within 5 business days of final approval, then pays it with the next payroll run.[1]
questions.expected: Within 5 business days of final approval, paid with the next payroll run.
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the reference and is directly supported by the cited reimbursement SLA.

questions.question: What's the deadline to submit an expense claim?
questions.answer: You must submit an expense claim within 30 days of the expense.[1] Expenses submitted more than 30 days late are non-reimbursable.[2]
questions.expected: Within 30 days of the expense.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the deadline stated in the in-force expense policy and matches the reference.

questions.question: How much is the employee referral bonus?
questions.answer: The employee referral bonus is $3,000 for a referral hired into a full-time role who completes 90 days of employment.[1] Referrals for intern and contract roles earn half the bonus.[2]
questions.expected: $3,000 once the hire completes 90 days (half for intern/contract roles).
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the reference: $3,000 after 90 days for full-time hires, with half for intern or contract roles.

questions.question: How long is the probation period for new hires?
questions.answer: New hires serve a 6-month introductory period, also called probation, from their start date.[1]

questions.question: How many days per week can I work from home?

questions.question: How much can I claim for home office equipment?
questions.answer: You can claim up to $1,000 once for home office equipment after the introductory period. It must be claimed through the expense system with receipts, and it is approved by your manager; the VP threshold does not apply.[1]
